title: Career roadmap · Digital Archivist
summary: A practical route from Digital Humanities and Cultural Studies into digital preservation, archives, metadata, cultural-heritage digitisation, records management, digital libraries and research-support roles.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a 4-year BA Honours pathway where applicable. A 3-year BA route can follow the same sequence by moving the final-year milestones one year earlier.

about.label: Route check
about.text: Digital Archivist is directly aligned with Digital Humanities / Cultural Studies.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build archival research, metadata, digitisation, digital humanities, documentation and basic technical skills.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Specialise in digital archives, cultural-heritage digitisation, digital libraries, records management or research data curation.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress into digital preservation, archive management, metadata leadership, collection strategy and cultural-heritage projects.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine archival expertise with AI-assisted discovery, digital preservation standards, linked data, OCR and large-scale cultural digitisation.

PhD routes
After a relevant master's degree, potential research areas include:
A PhD is particularly useful for academic research, university teaching, digital-humanities research and leadership of large cultural-heritage digitisation programmes.
2040–2046 relevance

Digital archives will increasingly use AI-assisted OCR, semantic search, automatic metadata extraction, linked open data, IIIF, digital-preservation systems and multimodal discovery. The valuable professional will be the person who can combine archival judgement with technology while protecting provenance, authenticity, context and long-term accessibility.
